title: Subset Counting for Multisets
description: Generalizes the subset counting theorem to multisets: a multiset with n elements has 2^n submultisets, and the number of k-element submultisets is C(n,k).

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib
originalContributions: Multiset powerset cardinality with pedagogical documentation
Fixed-size submultiset counting via binomial coefficients
Connection between Finset and Multiset powerset formulas
Concrete examples including multisets with repeated elements
meta.assumptions: None. Fully verified with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The multiset (or bag) is a fundamental data structure generalizing sets by allowing repeated elements. The powerset counting formula 2^n extends naturally to multisets when we count submultisets with multiplicity.
overview.problemStatement: How does |P(S)| = 2^n generalize to multisets? For a multiset s with n elements (counted with multiplicity), prove that the number of submultisets is 2^n and the number of k-element submultisets is C(n,k).
overview.text: Subset counting generalized to multisets via Mathlib's multiset powerset infrastructure.
overview.proofStrategy: Direct application of Mathlib's Multiset.card_powerset and Multiset.card_powersetCard, with pedagogical documentation connecting to the set case.
keyInsights: For multisets, each element occurrence is independently in or out of a submultiset, giving 2^n total
The number of DISTINCT submultisets (without multiplicity) is prod(m_i + 1) over distinct elements, where m_i is the multiplicity
When all multiplicities are 1 (i.e., a set), this reduces to 2^n

sections.title: Multiset Powerset Cardinality
sections.summary: Proves the multiset powerset has 2^n elements using Mathlib's card_powerset.

sections.title: Fixed-Size Submultisets
sections.summary: The number of k-element submultisets is C(n,k), the binomial coefficient.

sections.title: Connection to Set Case
sections.summary: Shows the multiset formula specializes to the set formula for Finsets.
sections.mathContext: For Finset s viewed as Multiset s.val, the powerset cardinality agrees.

sections.title: Concrete Examples
sections.summary: Examples: empty (1), singleton (2), triple (8), and C(4,2)=6.
sections.mathContext: Concrete verification with natural number multisets.

crossReferences.description: Generalizes the subset counting theorem from sets to multisets

conclusion.summary: A clean generalization of the subset counting theorem to multisets. 5 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, with concrete examples.
conclusion.implications: The multiset powerset formula is the foundation for generating function arguments in combinatorics.
openQuestions: Can we formalize the DISTINCT submultiset count prod(m_i + 1)?
How do multiset powerset operations connect to generating functions?

mainTheorems.name: multiset_powerset_card
mainTheorems.description: A multiset with n elements has 2^n submultisets
mainTheorems.leanType: (s : Multiset α) → card (powerset s) = 2 ^ card s

mainTheorems.name: multiset_choose_card
mainTheorems.description: The number of k-element submultisets is C(n, k)
mainTheorems.leanType: (s : Multiset α) → (k : ℕ) → card (powersetCard k s) = (card s).choose k
